'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Jerusalem shooting]]
**A [[Hamas]] gunman [[mass shooting|opens fire]] in the alleyways of [[Jerusalem]]'s [[Old City (Jerusalem)|Old City]], killing an [[Israelis|Israeli]] man and wounding three others, before being shot and killed by [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli forces]]. '''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Russia]]
****[[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] receives his [[booster dose]] of the [[Sputnik Light]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/russia/582565-putin-revaccinated-as-russias-vaccine-rate-remains-low (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] surpasses 400,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.urdupoint.com/en/health/slovenias-covid-19-cases-top-400000-1407083.html (''UrduPoint'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Guadeloupe]], [[Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***It is announced that [[government of France|France]] will deploy dozens of [[gendarmerie]] to [[Guadeloupe]] following occurrences of [[riot]]ing and [[looting]] in the [[archipelago]] over COVID-19 measures. At least 31 people were arrested overnight. [[Minister of the Interior (France)|Interior Minister]] [[Gérald Darmanin]] says that "the first message is that the state will stand firm". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/21/france-to-send-special-forces-to-guadeloupe-after-looting-arson (Al Jazeera)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
***[[Malaysia]] surpasses 30,000 deaths from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.malaymail.com/amp/news/malaysia/2021/11/22/with-24-new-covid-19-fatalities-malaysias-death-toll-goes-past-30000-mark/2022675 (''Malay Mail'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Waukesha Christmas parade attack]]
**Five people are killed and over 40 injured by a [[hit and run]] driver who drove through an early [[Christmas parade]] in [[Waukesha, Wisconsin]], [[United States]]. A [[person of interest]] is in custody. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/20-injured-car-drives-christmas-parade-wisconsin-police/story?id=81318232&cid=social_twitter_abcn (ABC News)]
*[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]]
**[[Belgian police]] fire [[tear gas]] and [[water cannon]]s after violence broke out at the end of a mass demonstration in [[Brussels]] that involved 35,000 people against tougher COVID-19-related measures. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/covid-news-live-booster-vaccine-b1961982.html?authId=1*qw9vzb*_a*WmNrWmFYNzN2d2h0bXd4Y2dSck1wV1I4djV6aGE5VzhxbzZZNkd0NmJWVmVTUUIzc1BoMXZscXRpTDZ0UHduMg..#post-521582 (''The Independent'')]
*The [[Taliban]] issues new guidelines for [[Television in Afghanistan|television]] broadcasts, mandating that female presenters and journalists wear [[Islamic clothing|Islamic coverings]], banning entertainment considered [[blasphemy law in Afghanistan|blasphemous]] or insulting to Afghans, and prohibiting films that promote foreign cultural values, among others. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-59368488 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Chilean general election]]
**[[Chileans]] go to the polls to elect their new [[President of Chile|president]], who will succeed outgoing president [[Sebastián Piñera]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/chileans-head-polls-with-two-radically-different-visions-ballot-2021-11-21/ (Reuters)]
**Far-right populist [[José Antonio Kast]] of the [[Republican Party (Chile, 2019)|Republican Party]] and former [[2011–2013 Chilean student protests|student protest]] leader [[Gabriel Boric]] of the left-wing coalition [[Apruebo Dignidad]] qualify for the second round, after winning 27.94% and 25.75% of the vote respectively. The second round will take place on December 19. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/chileans-head-polls-with-two-radically-different-visions-ballot-2021-11-21/ (Reuters)]
*Aftermath of the [[October 2021 Sudanese coup d'état]]
**[[Abdalla Hamdok]] is reinstated as [[Prime Minister of Sudan]] following a political agreement with coup leader [[Abdel Fattah al-Burhan]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-59364349 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 World Rally Championship]]
**[[Sébastien Ogier]] and [[Julien Ingrassia]] win the 2021 Championship, while [[Toyota Gazoo Racing WRT|Toyota]] secures the manufacturers' title.
